tasks.title: Export the uncut floor count from internal/engine
tasks.acceptance: internal/engine exports the uncut floor population as a function and internal/cli/ground.go's groundFloorSize calls it instead of duplicating the count, with lines_removed read on every edit. Verified by running on one fixture, a spec carrying cut units and no frontmatter: the exported function equals the line count of `tp ground <spec> --units` while the candidate-inclusive population does not. The closure states why neither engine.FloorUnits nor engine.FloorIndexRows was the answer, their difference being identically zero against real cut counts of 33, 15, 97, 53 and 6 across five specs, and says whether GroundCoverageOf's Emitted now calls the new function or stays separate.
tasks.closed_reason:
engine.FloorSize(rows []FloorIndexRow) int now exports the uncut floor population in internal/engine/floor.go -- it counts index rows carrying a hash, on 2.2's convention that the absence of the hash is the cut -- and internal/cli/ground.go's groundFloorSize is a one-line delegation to it, so the quantity has one definition serving both tp ground's floor_size and the lint field 2 specifies.
- Verified by running on one fixture, internal/cli's --units fixture (four candidate units, two cut by the arms, no frontmatter): tp ground spec.md --units prints 2 lines and engine.FloorSize returns 2, while the candidate-inclusive population is 4. TestFloorSizeIsTheUnitsListingsLineCount in internal/cli/ground_floor_size_test.go was written first and observed red twice -- once as undefined, then against a deliberate mutant body returning len(rows), which failed 4 against 2 and collapsed cut to 0, so the test discriminates the two populations instead of asserting a tautology. Re-measured on real specs, --units line count equals engine.FloorSize on spec/1.0.1.md (82), spec/0.37.0.md (173), spec/0.36.0.md (244) and spec/0.34.0.md (95).
- Neither engine.FloorUnits nor engine.FloorIndexRows was the answer: FloorUnits returns 2.1's candidate units with the arms' cuts included, and FloorIndexRows gives every candidate a row unconditionally because 2.2 announces the cut set, so their difference is identically zero. Re-derived here rather than inherited: the difference is 0 on all six specs measured (1.0.1, 0.37.0, 0.36.0, 0.35.0, 0.34.0, 0.31.1) whose real cut counts are 41, 53, 97, 100, 93 and 7.
- GroundCoverageOf's Emitted stays separate and does not call FloorSize. Emitted is the size of the emitted-id SET GroundCoverageOf must build anyway for its off-floor branch, and a set is not a row count: an index carrying one id twice would make FloorSize the larger of the two, and Dispositioned, which counts units, could then never reach it, breaking the bound Emitted's own doc states. The decision is recorded in FloorSize's doc comment so a later refactor does not collapse them.
- 2's table now names the derivation and the test in its last two columns, as 2 asks the implementing task to do, and its paragraph's claim that no exported function returns the uncut population is put in the past tense; review_panel's two columns stay task 4's. python3 scripts/check-spec-code-citations.py spec/1.0.1.md exits 0.
- Quality gate green: check-suite-state.sh 0, golangci-lint run 0, check-deadcode.sh 0, check-complexity.sh 0.

tasks.title: Split resolveRolePanel into resolver plus refusing wrapper
tasks.acceptance: resolveRolePanel becomes a pure resolution function plus a wrapper carrying the refusals and both output.Notice loops, and its two callers, internal/cli/review.go and internal/cli/audit.go, keep the wrapper with stdout, stderr and exit codes diffed identical before and after on the same tree, including the auditors-only refusal path. The task's first act is the decision section 7 asks for, since engine.roleUnits is already a pure resolution serving a read-only consumer: the closure says whether the shared pure half landed in internal/engine beside it or in internal/cli, and why a third copy was avoided. Tests are written red first and their names are then written into section 7, which currently says task 3 names them.
tasks.closed_reason:
The pure half landed in internal/engine as engine.ResolveRolePanel (internal/engine/rolepanel.go), not in internal/cli, and that was the task's first act. engine.roleUnits already held the same resolution for tp resume's read-only oracle, so a shared half in cli would have left that copy standing and made tp lint's the third — the shape §7 rejects. Putting it in engine instead reduced two copies to one: roleUnits now calls it, the cli wrapper calls it, and tp lint will be the third consumer of one resolution.
- The split: engine.ResolveRolePanel returns a RolePanel{Frontmatter, Roles, Disabled, Warnings} plus an error, and neither writes nor exits. internal/cli/resolveRolePanel keeps everything that refuses — the exit 3 abort on a malformed role file, the notice loop, refuseSpecCoverageDeactivated (auditors only) and refuseEmptyPhase — in §2.6's order. The cli rolePanel struct is unchanged, so review.go and audit.go are untouched by this commit series.
- Both callers diffed identical, not reasoned about. A 19-case command matrix over tp review and tp audit — both refusals, both notice loops in isolation and together (pinning their stderr order), the exit 3 malformed-role path in both phases, plain emission from a user corpus and from the embedded corpus, --role, --no-state and stateful runs, and the refusal-writes-nothing-to-disk check — was captured with a binary built at HEAD before the change and again after: stdout, stderr and exit code are byte-identical in all 19, including the auditors-only path (spec-coverage deactivated: exit 2 with the verbatim message, and the same when both refusals are armed, where spec-coverage still wins). tp resume was also diffed before/after on tp's own repo and on a review-phase fixture that exercises roleUnits: identical.
- The measurement §7 rests on was reproduced first, in a scratch fixture: on a corpus whose only reviewer declares domains: [prose] against a spec declaring domain: software, tp review writes exactly 86 bytes of notice to stderr and tp lint on the same tree writes none.
- Tests were written red first and the red was informative, not just a build error. After the compile failure I wrote the resolver as roleUnits' body promoted verbatim — the careless third-copy version — and watched two of the three engine tests fail for the reason expected: the corpus error came back nil and Warnings came back nil. Test 1 passed against that draft, which is recorded in §7: it does not stand alone.
- Three mutants were then built against the finished code and reverted: moving the notice loop into the resolver (engine test 3 fails on non-empty stderr; the cli test's review byte count goes 86 to 172), dropping refuseSpecCoverageDeactivated from the wrapper (the cli spec-coverage sub-test fails), and moving the empty-phase refusal into the resolver (engine test 1 does not fail — it kills the package test binary, which is the observable form of the defect).
- §7 now records the decision inline in its alternatives paragraph and replaces its 'Task 3 names them' placeholder with a table naming TestResolveRolePanel_ResolvesAnEmptiedPhaseWithoutRefusing, TestResolveRolePanel_ReturnsTheCorpusErrorInsteadOfExiting, TestResolveRolePanel_ReturnsWarningsWithoutWritingThem (internal/engine) and TestRolePanelWrapper_RefusalsAndNoticesStayOnTheWrapper (internal/cli), plus the three mutants and the honest note that row 1 does not discriminate alone.
- The two-caller claim was counted, not assumed: a search for resolveRolePanel across the repository returns its definition plus exactly two call sites, internal/cli/review.go:569 and internal/cli/audit.go:306.
- Quality gate, each step's exit code read separately: check-suite-state.sh 0, golangci-lint run 0 (0 issues), check-deadcode.sh 0, check-complexity.sh 0. Dogfooded with a freshly built /tmp/tp-dev/tp: tp lint spec/1.0.1.md exit 0 with 0 issues, tp resume exit 0.
Out of scope: tp lint does not call the resolver yet — the review_panel field and lint's empty-stderr guarantee are the next task's. The cli test pins lint's empty stderr today as a baseline, and the test comment says so rather than claiming it discriminates.

tasks.title: tp lint reports review_panel
tasks.acceptance: `tp lint <spec>` emits review_panel as a JSON list of reviewer role ids equal to those a round-1 `tp review <spec>` emission with no --diff-from carries, obtained through resolver-split's pure function so that lint gains no second derivation. Section 6 row 2 is written first and observed red on its constructed fixture, a temporary corpus in which exactly one role declares domains and a spec whose frontmatter does not match, reproducing the recorded counts of one role at HEAD against two under the mutant. No test asserts parity across this repository's own corpus, because no reviewer role in it declares domains and the filter is therefore inert, which round 2 measured as zero domain-mismatch skips over every spec.
tasks.closed_reason:
tp lint <spec> now emits review_panel, the reviewer role ids a round-1 tp review emission of the same spec carries with no --diff-from. It is one derivation, not two: lintReviewPanel in internal/cli/lint.go calls engine.ResolveRolePanel, the pure half §7's split created, and never the refusing wrapper -- so lint neither refuses a spec nor gains the wrapper's two advisory output.Notice loops. The ids are built with make([]string, 0), so an empty panel answers [] rather than null.
- The test was written first and observed red twice, and the second red is the informative one. Red 1 was the absent field. Red 2 was §6 row 2's own named mutant, resolve the corpus but skip the domain filter, built in an rsync copy as if true in ResolveActiveCorpus: it reproduces the recorded counts exactly, ["universal"] at HEAD against ["prose-only", "universal"] under the mutant, and it now fails on the row's own assertion rather than on a fixture guard -- the first draft caught it at a require precondition instead, so the assertions were reordered until the failure message is the requirement.
- A second mutant was built and reverted to prove the equality assertion is not decoration: lint deriving the panel itself from engine.LoadRoleCorpus with no domain filter leaves the emission at ["universal"] and lint at ["prose-only", "universal"], and the Equal fails. So a mutant in the shared resolver is caught by the NotContains and a mutant that gives lint a second derivation is caught by the Equal.
- The fixture is built for the row, and its own precondition is asserted rather than trusted: exactly one of its two reviewer roles declares domains, because a second would empty the panel and send tp to the embedded default corpus. This repository's corpus cannot serve -- no role in .tp/reviewers declares domains, the filter is inert here, and a test over it could not fail. No test asserts parity across it.
- Dogfooded with a freshly built /tmp/tp-dev/tp. On spec/1.0.1.md in the repo, review_panel is [architect, ax-economist, implementer, tester] with floor_size 90 and cut 43, lint stderr empty; tp review on that spec cannot emit (its round budget is exhausted at 2), so parity was measured on the same spec and the same corpus relocated to a temp dir: lint and a round-1 tp review emission both report [architect, ax-economist, implementer, tester]. The empty-panel edge, which is the next task's, already answers review_panel [] on a spec deactivating its only reviewer.
- §2's review_panel row now names engine.ResolveRolePanel through lintReviewPanel in internal/cli/lint.go, and TestLintReviewPanelOmitsADomainMismatchedRole in internal/cli/lint_review_panel_test.go for §6 row 2, saying plainly that row 3's fixture ships with the empty-panel task rather than claiming two fixtures this task did not write. The paragraph's forward reference is put in the past tense. python3 scripts/check-spec-code-citations.py spec/1.0.1.md exits 0.
- TestLintPayloadIsByteIdenticalUnderCompactAndQuiet was run and passes with the new field present.
- Quality gate, each step's exit code read separately: check-suite-state.sh 0, golangci-lint run 0 (0 issues), check-deadcode.sh 0, check-complexity.sh 0.

source_sections: ## 3. The fence and the inline span
tasks.closed_reason:
- Row 8 is pinned by TestBrokenCrossRefStillReportsWhereVagueLanguageIsSilent in internal/engine/vague_fence_test.go, on the fixture that separates: a backticked `§1.1 step 5` reference whose target section holds a two-item numbered list, on the same line as a backticked trigger word. Measured at HEAD, vague-language 0 and broken-cross-ref 1; under the mutant -- blankInlineCode inserted into CheckBrokenCrossRefs, built in an rsync -a copy of the tree -- vague-language 0 and broken-cross-ref 0. The test was observed red there before it was accepted, failing at vague_fence_test.go:189 on the require.Len that carries the requirement ("[] should have 1 item(s), but has 0"), not on any of the three fixture preconditions, which stay green under that mutant by design. Those preconditions are derived from the fixture rather than asserted about it: the referenced step is read back out of the line with crossRefSectionStep and required to exceed a sectionStepCounts value that is itself required positive, which is exactly what the listless target this row carried for two rounds fails.

One figure elsewhere did need correcting, and it was found by the same run: 13.3's closing paragraph says row 4's mutant sends rows 4, 5 and 7 all from 0 to 1, while the failing tests are rows 4, 6 and 7 and only row 4's goes 0 to 1 -- row 5's fixture contains no fence, so a fence-only mutant cannot move it, measured 0 under it. 13.4 records the correction and leaves the paragraph's surviving half standing.

tasks.title: Ship the spec-writing rules to SKILL.md
tasks.acceptance: Every bullet in section 4 except the last, which is precedent, lands in skills/tp/SKILL.md, and the closure gives the count it derived from the bullet list rather than restating a number the spec does not carry. The fenced-command rule as shipped names both the interpreter and the binary, since naming bash alone leaves the binary free and round 2 recorded that gap. For each rule the closure states whether an author can check it while writing or only after a grading round, because a rule judgeable only afterwards costs rounds rather than saving them.
tasks.closed_reason:
Shipped section 4's rules to skills/tp/SKILL.md as "Step 0.5: Writing the spec body", placed between Step 0 (Interview) and Step 1 (Init) and split under three subheadings so no section crosses the 50-line section-size limit; Workflow A's order line now reads interview -> write the spec body -> tp lint -> ... .

- Count derived, not restated. `awk 'NR>=154 && NR<=204' spec/1.0.1.md | grep -c '^- '` returns 8 top-level bullets and `grep -c '^- Already shipped, cited as precedent'` returns 1, so 8 - 1 = 7 new rules. The shipped block returns 7 for `grep -c '^- \*\*'` over lines 55-110 of SKILL.md, one bolded bullet per rule: numbers-vs-references, fenced commands, ADR shape, test-row mutants, unchanged-behaviour sentences, grading briefs, check prototypes. A first draft split the test-row rule across two bullets and made the shipped count 8 - exactly the miscount section 4 warns about - so the two clauses were merged back into one bullet before commit.
- The fenced-command rule names both the interpreter and the binary, as two named sub-bullets. Interpreter: invoke each block as `bash -c '<block>'`, because a block that printed seventeen rows under bash printed nothing at exit 0 under zsh, which reads "$tag:..." as a history modifier. Binary: build the tree's own binary and call it by path (`go build -o /tmp/tp-dev/tp ./cmd/tp`, then `/tmp/tp-dev/tp ...`), because a bare `tp` resolves against PATH, which lags the tree, so the block would certify a release the spec is not about.
- Check-point judgement, recorded for every rule: all seven are answerable while writing and none needs a grading round. Numbers-vs-references, ADR shape, the unchanged-behaviour scope test, the brief-repeats-no-figure rule and the check-prototype rule are each a judgement on the author's own text; the fenced-command rule is mechanical and runnable before any round. One exception is stated in the shipped text: a test row whose subject does not exist at HEAD has its form and fixture checkable while writing, but its two counts are confirmable only once the code lands - still before the first grading round, so it belongs in the implementing task's acceptance rather than in a round's rows.

Verification: `tp lint skills/tp/SKILL.md` is unchanged from the pre-edit baseline - 0 errors, 7 warnings (the same 5 vague-language plus the 2 pre-existing section-size) and 33 info, so the new sections add no finding. Quality gate all four steps exit 0: check-suite-state.sh 0, golangci-lint run 0, check-deadcode.sh 0, check-complexity.sh 0.

tasks.title: Document the three lint fields for release
tasks.acceptance: README.md documents the three fields tp lint adds, and .claude-plugin/plugin.json's version is bumped before any tag. The release notes state the case the cycle measured, that review_panel replaces an emission with a lint invocation, and cite spec/1.0.1-measurements.md section 11 for the byte counts rather than quoting them. They also say plainly that the release shipped with its review round unconverged at its cap, and why: five grading rounds refuted five successive sets of sentences about code that did not exist yet.
tasks.closed_reason:
Three criteria, each measured rather than asserted.

- Criterion 1 — README.md's Spec Quality section now names floor_size, cut and review_panel in a three-row table placed after the tp review paragraph, where both tp ground and tp review have already been introduced. The three keys were derived from the shipped binary, not from the spec: tp lint spec/1.0.1.md --json returns exactly ['cut','errors','file','findings','floor_size','frontmatter','info','review_panel','structured_elements','warnings'], with floor_size 96, cut 43, review_panel ['architect','ax-economist','implementer','tester']. Every claim in the table was run: tp ground spec/1.0.1.md --units prints 96 lines against floor_size 96 (and left spec/.tp-review/1.0.1/state.json md5-identical, so --units persists nothing); the payload is byte-identical under --json, --json --compact and --json --quiet (same md5 three times), which is what "on every invocation" rests on. tp lint README.md reports the same three findings before and after the edit (one pre-existing orphan-reference on the rule table's own example row, two pre-existing section-size warnings) — no new finding class; the Spec Quality section-size warning moved from 100 to 116 lines and it already carried that warning. No SKILL.md inventory and no REFERENCE.md field detail is restated: the floor_size distinction is linked, not copied.

- Criterion 2 — spec/1.0.1-release-notes.md states the case as the cycle measured it: review_panel is the one field with no cheap alternative, because learning a round-1 panel used to mean emitting the round, and lint answers it from a resolver that writes nothing. The byte counts are cited to spec/1.0.1-measurements.md section 11 and are not quoted, which is also the rule section 4 of the spec ships. The notes name what did not ship — floor_by_section, spec_bytes and floor_figure_share — each with the measurement that refuted it and a pointer to spec/undecided.md for the reopen condition, and record that six candidate smell rules were prototyped and all six refuted.

- Criterion 3 — the notes say plainly that tp review spec/1.0.1.md recorded two rounds against a cap of two and did not converge, and give the reason in one sentence: five grading rounds — three grounding, one review, one delta pass — refuted five successive sets of sentences about code that did not exist yet. Every quantifier was counted rather than repeated. spec/.tp-review/1.0.1/ holds ground-round-{1,2,3}.ndjson and review-round-{1,2}.ndjson, so five grading rounds; state.json records review rounds 1 and 2 with clean:false; tp config --resolved reports review_max_rounds 2 from the task-file override; tp review --status reports converged:false and budget_exhausted:true; and tp review spec/1.0.1.md --no-state now exits 4 with "review round budget exhausted" and prints nothing to stdout. The notes point at section 14 for what implementation corrected rather than narrating the cycle.

- Plugin version verified rather than assumed. .claude-plugin/plugin.json says 1.0.1; git describe --tags --abbrev=0 is v1.0.0. TestPluginVersionIsNotBehindTheLatestTag asserts manifest >= latest tag, which 1.0.1 >= 1.0.0 satisfies; TestPluginVersionIsBumpedWhenPluginContentChanges asserts manifest > tag whenever anything under .claude-plugin/, skills/, hooks/ or agents/ has moved since the tag, which this cycle's SKILL.md and REFERENCE.md commits make true, and 1.0.1 > 1.0.0 satisfies that too. No bump was needed; the field was already correct.

- Two corrections to what this task was handed. Section 11's own derivation command no longer reproduces on spec/1.0.1.md at HEAD: the review budget is exhausted, so tp review spec/1.0.1.md --no-state exits 4 and writes nothing to stdout, and the magnitude survives only on a spec with rounds left (spec/1.0.2.md emits 22,752 bytes against section 11's 22,181). That is why the notes cite the section instead of the numbers. And section 14's "nine corrections across seven tasks" is nine rows over six distinct task ids in its own task column — the count of tasks is not derivable from the table it sits beside, so the notes point at the section without repeating either figure.

- Quality gate run in four separate invocations, each exit code read on its own: check-suite-state.sh 0, golangci-lint run 0 (0 issues), check-deadcode.sh 0, check-complexity.sh 0. Committed with hc as two commits, one per file. No tag, no push, no release was created: publishing is the operator's decision.

tasks.title: REFERENCE.md distinguishes the two floor_size quantities
tasks.acceptance: skills/tp/REFERENCE.md states that lint's floor_size is the live text's floor while the floor_size in tp review's ungrounded envelope is the latest emitted round's frozen index, and gives the condition under which they agree. The paragraph is written after lint's field exists so that both quantities can be run and compared rather than described, and the closure quotes the two numbers it saw diverge on one spec.
tasks.closed_reason:
- Criterion 1 — REFERENCE.md gains "### `floor_size` — one name, two quantities" at the end of the Grounding section, right after the paragraph that already equates `tp ground --status`'s `emitted` with `ungrounded.floor_size`. It states that all three `floor_size` keys count uncut floor units and differ only in the text counted: `tp lint`'s is the spec as it stands on disk, `tp review`'s `ungrounded.floor_size` (and `--status`'s `emitted`) is the latest emitted round's frozen index, and `tp ground <spec>`'s emission envelope is where the two coincide by construction; `cut` splits the same way.
